correctness.rationale: The odd-prime-power lemma is proved by parity for even exponents and by factoring beta(q^(2u-1))=(q-1)*(1+q^2+...+q^(2u-2)) for odd exponents: any u>1 forces an odd factor. Thus beta(m) a power of two for odd m forces squarefree Fermat-prime support. If n=p^a solves the iterated equation then p=2. For even a, order(2 modulo Fermat primes) rules out every factor beyond F0, forcing a=2. For odd a, writing a+1=2^t*v with v odd forces all Fermat factors to have index <t and hence v=1 by size; F5 composite forces t<=5. Direct finite factorization proves the converse. The independent standard-library verifier confirms 510 local cases, 24 exponents, exponent 31, and the finite Fermat input, without substituting experiments for the proof.

value.rationale: Tóth explicitly poses the existence of further super-imperfect numbers as an open problem. The prime powers p^a form an intrinsic, complete multiplicative class, and the theorem excludes *every* possible further candidate in it, not merely a predetermined set of exponents or a finite computational interval. A clean Fermat-prime support obstruction explains why the six observed examples exhaust the class and provides a usable reduction for future investigations of the remaining multi-prime case. The result does not claim the full open problem is solved.
